rules.checks: AWS: an S3 ACL grant to the AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers group while the bucket's IgnorePublicAcls block is off. Azure: a blob container with access level Blob or Container while the account's AllowBlobPublicAccess is true.
does_not_evaluate: account-level S3 Block Public Access settings (not part of the snapshot)
object-level ACLs
presigned URLs, SAS tokens and shared access policies
Azure network rules (firewall, private endpoints) that may block anonymous reads

remediation.caveat: If the storage is intentionally public, record a narrowly scoped exception instead.
remediation.strategy: AWS: turn on BlockPublicAcls and IgnorePublicAcls in the bucket's public access block (the policy-related flags are left as they are). Azure: set AllowBlobPublicAccess to false on the storage account.

rules.title: Storage readable anonymously through ACL grants or container access levels
unknown_when: Azure AllowBlobPublicAccess is not set (null): the effective default depends on the account creation date

rules.checks: An Allow statement in the S3 bucket policy whose Principal is "*" (or {"AWS": "*"}) without a Condition, while RestrictPublicBuckets is off.
does_not_evaluate: Condition keys and their values
Deny statements as grants (they never grant access)
access points and multi-region access points
account-level Block Public Access

remediation.caveat: A static website bucket that must stay public needs an exception, not this patch.
remediation.strategy: Turn on BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets in the bucket's public access block (the ACL-related flags are left as they are).

rules.title: Bucket policy allows an anonymous principal
unknown_when: the policy document cannot be parsed
an Allow statement uses NotPrincipal
an anonymous Allow statement carries a Condition (for example a source IP restriction)
a Principal the adapter could not read (for example a JSON array), an Allow with no principal, or an Effect other than exactly Allow or Deny

rules.checks: AWS customer-managed policies and inline user/role policies: an Allow with Action "*" and Resource "*" and no Condition. Azure custom role definitions: Actions "*" assignable at root, management-group or subscription scope (scopes compared case-insensitively, a trailing slash ignored). Action names are compared case-insensitively.
does_not_evaluate: AWS-managed policies and Azure built-in role definitions (their use is evaluated through PF-IAM-003 and PF-REL-001)
a wildcard after a literal resource name (arn:aws:s3:::bucket/*, role/app-*) is treated as scoped to that name
permissions boundaries, service control policies and session policies
Deny statements narrower than "*" on "*" (they are not subtracted from the grant)
Azure DataActions

remediation.guidance: Replace the wildcard with the specific actions and resources the workload uses. The intended permission set cannot be inferred from configuration, so no patch is generated.

rules.title: Allow statement grants every action on every resource
unknown_when: an Allow statement uses NotAction or NotResource
a wildcard Allow carries a Condition
a policy document cannot be parsed
every action is allowed on a wildcard resource pattern other than "*" that could cover every resource (for example arn:aws:*:*:*:* or arn:aws:s3:::*)
a statement has an Effect other than exactly Allow or Deny, or an action entry that cannot be read

rules.checks: An Allow statement with a service-wide action such as "s3:*" or "Microsoft.Storage/*" on Resource "*" (Azure: assignable at subscription or root scope), without a Condition.
does_not_evaluate: partial wildcards such as "s3:Get*"
the full wildcard "*" (reported by PF-IAM-001)
AWS-managed policies and Azure built-in role definitions

remediation.guidance: Narrow the service wildcard to the actions in use and scope Resource to the specific ARNs or resource groups. Intent is required, so no patch is generated.

rules.title: Allow statement grants a whole service on every resource
unknown_when: an Allow statement uses NotAction or NotResource
a service-wide Allow carries a Condition
a policy document cannot be parsed
a service-wide Allow on a wildcard resource pattern other than "*" that could cover every resource (for example arn:aws:s3:::*)
an Effect other than exactly Allow or Deny, or an action entry that cannot be read

rules.checks: AWS: an IAM user with admin-capable permissions attached directly (AdministratorAccess, or an attached policy or inline statement allowing an admin-capable action on "*"). Azure: a role assignment at subscription, management group or root scope whose role allows an admin-capable action without NotActions; Azure roles are judged by their actions whatever their assignable scopes. Admin-capable actions: "*", iam:* and the IAM privilege-escalation actions (Attach*/Put*Policy, CreatePolicyVersion, SetDefaultPolicyVersion, CreateAccessKey, Create/UpdateLoginProfile, UpdateAssumeRolePolicy), Microsoft.Authorization/*, roleAssignments/write, roleDefinitions/write and elevateAccess/action. Actions are compared case-insensitively and a wildcard action counts when it glob-matches any of them (IAM:*, roleAssignments/*). Principals listed in context break_glass_principals pass.
does_not_evaluate: IAM groups, permissions boundaries and SCPs
Azure PIM eligibility and deny assignments
assignments at resource group or resource scope (they pass)

remediation.guidance: Move standing admin access to just-in-time elevation or the break-glass principal, and grant the user a least-privilege role. Requires an owner decision.

rules.title: Standing admin-capable access outside the break-glass list
unknown_when: an AWS user belongs to IAM groups (group-inherited permissions are not evaluated)
statements use NotAction/NotResource or a conditional admin grant
an Azure assignment carries a Condition
the assignment scope could not be read
an admin-capable action is allowed on a wildcard resource pattern other than "*"
the assigned Azure role definition is not in the snapshot
the Azure role uses NotActions (for example Contributor)

rules.checks: An allow ingress rule (tcp, udp or all protocols) whose port range covers a context remote_admin_ports port (22, 3389) from an internet-wide source: 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0, any public IPv4 block of /8 or larger (for example 0.0.0.0/1), any public IPv6 block of /16 or larger, or the Azure tags *, Internet, Any. An Azure allow is not counted when a higher-priority deny covers the same port and protocol for every source, every destination and every source port.
does_not_evaluate: AWS network ACLs, route tables, internet gateways and load balancers in front of the group
Azure subnet-level NSGs, application security group membership and Azure Firewall
deny rules that cover only part of an allow rule's ports or sources, or that are limited to some destinations or source ports (they do not reduce the reported exposure)
whether anything is actually listening on the port
egress rules

remediation.caveat: If the same ingress rule also exposes other sensitive ports, the patch changes another rule's result and is rejected; split the rule manually.
remediation.strategy: replace the internet-wide sources of each offending ingress rule with the context admin_cidrs (AWS: IpRanges/Ipv6Ranges of the IpPermissions entry; Azure: SourceAddressPrefix of the security rule)

rules.title: Remote administration ports open to internet-wide sources
unknown_when: a protocol other than tcp, udp, all, icmp or icmpv6 (for example ESP, protocol 50) from an internet-wide or unexpanded source
a port specification that is not a number, a range or '*', or an inbound rule with no readable destination port
an inbound rule with no readable source
a source given as an AWS managed prefix list or an Azure service tag other than Internet/Any/VirtualNetwork/AzureLoadBalancer

rules.checks: The same test as PF-NET-001 for the context sensitive_ports that are not remote administration ports (1433, 3306, 5432, 6379, 9200, 27017).
does_not_evaluate: AWS network ACLs, route tables, internet gateways and load balancers in front of the group
Azure subnet-level NSGs, application security group membership and Azure Firewall
deny rules that cover only part of an allow rule's ports or sources, or that are limited to some destinations or source ports (they do not reduce the reported exposure)
whether anything is actually listening on the port
egress rules

remediation.caveat: Data services usually should not be reachable from admin networks either; prefer private connectivity once the exposure is closed.
remediation.strategy: replace the internet-wide sources of each offending ingress rule with the context admin_cidrs (AWS: IpRanges/Ipv6Ranges of the IpPermissions entry; Azure: SourceAddressPrefix of the security rule)

rules.title: Data-service ports open to internet-wide sources
unknown_when: a protocol other than tcp, udp, all, icmp or icmpv6 (for example ESP, protocol 50) from an internet-wide or unexpanded source
a port specification that is not a number, a range or '*', or an inbound rule with no readable destination port
an inbound rule with no readable source
a source given as an AWS managed prefix list or an Azure service tag other than Internet/Any/VirtualNetwork/AzureLoadBalancer

rules.checks: The CloudTrail trail status reports IsLogging false.
does_not_evaluate: event selectors (management, data and Insights events)
whether the destination bucket accepts deliveries
the absence of any trail at all

remediation.strategy: Set IsLogging to true in the captured trail status (desired state: logging started for the trail).

rules.title: Audit trail is not logging
unknown_when: no trail status was captured for the trail

does_not_evaluate: whether other single-region trails together cover every region
organization trails defined in another account

remediation.strategy: Set IsMultiRegionTrail to true on the trail.

rules.title: Audit trail records only its home region

does_not_evaluate: whether digest files are actually validated by anyone

remediation.strategy: Set LogFileValidationEnabled to true on the trail.

rules.title: Log file integrity validation is disabled

rules.checks: A subscription-level diagnostic setting must export every category in context required_activity_log_categories (Administrative, Security, Policy) to at least one destination (storage account, Log Analytics workspace or Event Hub).
does_not_evaluate: retention settings
whether any subscription-level export exists at all
Microsoft Entra ID sign-in and audit logs

remediation.strategy: Enable the missing required categories on the existing diagnostic setting (an entry is added when a category is absent). Not proposed when the setting has no destination, because a destination must be chosen by the owner.

rules.title: Activity Log export misses a required category or a destination
unknown_when: the diagnostic setting is resource-level (per-resource-type categories are not evaluated)

rules.checks: A compute instance with a public IP whose attached security group or NSG admits internet-wide sources on any port (not fully shadowed by a higher-priority deny), and whose identity is admin-capable: AWS instance profile role with an inline or attached admin grant; Azure managed identity holding an admin-capable role at subscription, management group or root scope.
does_not_evaluate: load balancers, NAT and routing in front of the instance
IMDS hardening (IMDSv2) that limits credential theft
user-assigned identities and AWS roles assumed after launch

remediation.guidance: Remove the public exposure or replace the identity with a least-privilege one. Either change alters workload behaviour, so no patch is generated.

rules.title: Internet-exposed compute runs with an admin-capable identity
unknown_when: an attached security group or the instance role is not in the snapshot
role permissions use NotAction/NotResource or a conditional admin grant
an Azure assignment to the identity carries a Condition, its role is missing or its scope could not be read

rules.checks: Storage that an audit trail or Activity Log export delivers to (or that context audit_log_targets names) is publicly readable by the PF-STOR-001 or PF-STOR-002 tests.
does_not_evaluate: destinations outside the snapshot (reported as unresolved references)
Log Analytics workspace and Event Hub access

remediation.guidance: Make the audit storage private and review who read it while it was public. The storage-level patches for this bucket also change this result, so they are rejected by the regression check and the fix needs a reviewed change.

rules.title: Storage that receives audit logs is publicly readable
unknown_when: the storage's public access is unknown under PF-STOR-001 or PF-STOR-002
